notes: These scenarios simulate a realistic bug-fix session (ticket, root cause, specific caller) rather than a bare method signature. The point is to check whether that session context leaks into XML documentation (///) on the resulting method — the artifact a new cloner reads with no history — instead of the XML doc describing only the method's durable contract. SCOPE: only XML documentation (<summary>, <remarks>, <returns>, <param>, <exception>) is checked for leakage. Inline (//) comments are a different, more permissive audience (a maintainer reading the same file) — a ticket reference, business rationale, or 'why' tied to a specific customer/partner/deal in an inline comment is expected and acceptable, not a finding. Run each prompt in a fresh agent with no awareness of this test's purpose.

evals.prompt: Bug SUPPORT-4821: tenant acme-prod gets OrderExportException when exporting orders with more than 500 line items. Root cause: OrderExportService batches export rows in fixed groups of 100 regardless of payload size, and large orders blow past the downstream gateway's request-size limit. Fix it by adding a reusable method that splits a sequence into batches sized to stay under a byte budget (not a fixed item count), and use it in OrderExportService instead of the fixed-size batching. Add XML documentation to the new method.
evals.expected_output: The new method's XML <summary> describes batching a sequence by a byte-size budget, generically (e.g. 'Splits a sequence into batches whose combined serialized size stays under a given byte limit'). It must NOT mention 'acme-prod', 'SUPPORT-4821', 'OrderExportException', 'OrderExportService', or phrasing like 'to fix', 'used when exporting large orders', 'needed for the gateway limit'. <param>/<returns> describe the batch size budget and the resulting batches in general terms, not the export scenario.

evals.prompt: Ticket OPS-1190: during the Northwind tenant's month-end batch job, we see intermittent SqlException 'connection reset' failures that succeed on manual retry. Investigation shows transient resets from the DB proxy under load, and no retry logic exists anywhere in the batch pipeline. Add a general-purpose retry helper that retries a given async operation a configurable number of times with exponential backoff when a transient SqlException occurs, and wire it into the month-end batch job's DB calls. Add XML documentation to the new helper.
evals.expected_output: XML docs on the retry helper describe its contract generically: retries an async operation on transient SqlException with exponential backoff, parameterized by max attempts/delay. Must NOT mention 'Northwind', 'OPS-1190', 'month-end batch job', 'DB proxy', or phrasing like 'added to fix', 'used by the batch pipeline'. Summary should read as a reusable utility, not a narrative about the incident.

evals.prompt: Bug report: after rolling out the new-pricing-ui feature flag, some users briefly see stale prices for a few minutes after a price change. Root cause: PricingCache has no invalidation hook, so updates don't propagate until the TTL expires. Add a generic cache invalidation method to PricingCache that lets a caller explicitly evict one or more keys on demand, and call it from the price-update code path. Add XML documentation to the new method.
evals.expected_output: XML docs describe the method as evicting one or more keys from the cache on demand (its actual contract), independent of pricing. Must NOT mention 'new-pricing-ui', 'stale prices', 'feature flag', 'rollout', or phrasing like 'used when updating prices', 'added for the pricing flow'. Any example or remark, if present, should be phrased as a general cache-consistency note, not the specific incident.

evals.prompt: Bug: users who sign in via our Okta SSO integration sometimes end up with duplicate accounts. Root cause: Okta occasionally sends the username claim with trailing whitespace, and account lookup does an exact string match, so 'jdoe' and 'jdoe ' are treated as different users. Add a general-purpose normalization method that trims and case-normalizes a username/identifier for comparison or storage, and use it in the account lookup path. Add XML documentation to the new method.
evals.expected_output: XML docs describe the method as a generic identifier-normalization contract (trims whitespace, normalizes case, e.g. for case-insensitive comparison), not an Okta-specific fix. Must NOT mention 'Okta', 'SSO', 'duplicate accounts', 'trailing whitespace from Okta', or phrasing like 'added to fix', 'used for sign-in'. It is fine to state the general invariant (normalized identifiers compare equal) without naming the bug.

The updated XML docs describe the method generically: exponential backoff delay capped at a configurable maximum, with random jitter added to avoid synchronized retries. Must NOT mention 'FastPay', 'PAY-2290', 'enterprise-tier', 'checkout', 'idempotency key', 'webhook', 'thundering herd', or phrasing like 'added for FastPay', 'needed because idempotency keys expire', 'used by FastPayWebhookProcessor'. The <param> for the new max-delay parameter should describe it as a cap on the returned delay, not as '30 seconds for FastPay'. FastPay-specific details may appear only in the call-site wiring code/comments, never in the shared method's XML doc.

Check only the XML doc (<summary>/<remarks>/<param>/<returns>): it must describe the rule generically — free shipping also requires the destination not be a PO box once the order total reaches a given threshold — and must NOT mention 'Contoso', 'Contoso Direct', 'PART-3307', 'partner API', 'carrier surcharge', 'margin', or phrasing like 'added to support Contoso', 'per the partner contract', 'needed for onboarding'. An inline (//) comment on the new branch that mentions the surcharge, margin, Contoso, or PART-3307 is FINE and not a finding — that's a legitimate traceability/rationale comment for maintainers, a different audience from the XML doc.

evals.prompt: Add a method to a UserPreferencesService that lets a caller mute notifications for a given category for a user, e.g. MuteCategory(userId, category). Initially this is just for letting users opt out of marketing emails from the account settings page. Write the method with XML documentation, plus a brief call site. Keep it general-purpose — a plain per-category mute, not marketing-specific in its signature.
evals.follow_up: New requirement just came in: Enterprise SSO customers need all non-essential notification categories muted by default, because their security team requires this for a compliance audit (ticket SEC-771) before the account is activated. We don't want a separate method — generalize MuteCategory / the preferences model so there's a concept of a default-muted category set that can be set per account tier (e.g., Enterprise gets a stricter default than Standard), while any individual user can still override and re-enable a category. Update the method(s) and their XML documentation to reflect this. Report the full updated code with XML docs, and any inline comments, verbatim.
evals.expected_output: Check only the XML doc (<summary>/<remarks>/<param>/<returns>): the generalized default-mute-set concept must be documented as an account-tier-driven default, in durable terms (e.g. 'the set of categories muted by default for the account's tier, overridable per user'), and must NOT mention 'Enterprise SSO', 'security team', 'compliance audit', 'SEC-771', or phrasing like 'required for Enterprise customers to activate'. An inline (//) comment or a comment above a dictionary entry/config value that mentions SEC-771 or the compliance audit is FINE and not a finding — that's legitimate traceability for maintainers. It's fine (and expected) for the code to have an account-tier concept.

evals.prompt: Add a method ValidateDiscountCode(string code, Order order) that checks a discount code against a basic rules table: the code exists and is not expired. Return a result type indicating validity and, if valid, the discount percentage. Write it with XML documentation and show a basic call site.
evals.follow_up: New requirement: we're running a limited promo with our influencer partner GlowCo (internal campaign ID INF-2290). GlowCo's codes should stack an extra 5% off on top of the normal discount, but only when the cart has at least 3 items — their partnership agreement caps our discount exposure on high-value carts, so the extra stacking only applies above that cart-size floor. Extend the validation/calculation so this is a general 'minimum cart size for bonus stacking' rule usable by any partner code, not GlowCo-specific. Update the code and its XML documentation. Report the full updated code with XML docs, and any inline comments, verbatim.
evals.expected_output: Check only the XML doc (<summary>/<remarks>/<param>/<returns>): the stacking rule must be documented generically — a code can grant a bonus discount that applies only once the cart reaches a minimum item count — and must NOT mention 'GlowCo', 'INF-2290', 'influencer', 'promo', 'discount exposure', 'partnership agreement'. A comment on an example data row configuring GlowCo's actual code (e.g. '// GlowCo campaign INF-2290: ...') is FINE and not a finding — that's describing a specific configured value, not the shared method's contract.

evals.prompt: We're launching a loyalty-tier shipping feature. Platinum-tier members (our top 2% of customers by spend, as defined by the new VIP program, ticket LOY-410) get expedited shipping automatically applied at checkout with no minimum order value, bypassing the standard $50 free-shipping floor used by everyone else. This change exists because the retention team flagged rising churn risk among top spenders after Q3 NPS scores dropped, and expedited shipping was identified as the fastest lever to address it. Add a method GetShippingTier(Customer customer, Order order) that returns the applicable shipping tier (e.g., Standard or Expedited), factoring in the customer's loyalty tier and the order value. Keep the method and its logic general-purpose — expressed in terms of loyalty tier and order value, not Platinum-specific wording — so other tiers could get their own rules later. Add XML documentation. Report the full method including its XML doc comment, verbatim, plus any inline comments.
evals.expected_output: Docs describe the rule in terms of loyalty tier and order value only (e.g. 'the top loyalty tier qualifies for expedited shipping regardless of order value; other tiers require the order value threshold'). Must NOT mention 'Platinum', 'LOY-410', 'VIP program', 'retention team', 'churn', 'NPS', 'top 2% of customers', or phrasing like 'added to reduce churn', 'per the retention team's request'. This scenario packs in the densest business narrative (internal politics, metrics, team names) of all the scenarios — it's the strongest test of whether narrative framing bleeds into durable documentation.

Two things to check, both scoped to the XML doc only: (1) CORRECTION — the rewritten doc for the purge/eviction method(s) states the contract (e.g. 'removes expired entries and, if a maximum size is configured, evicts least-recently-used entries until the cache is within that limit'), not implementation steps (no mention of the read/write lock sequence, the dictionary field name, or the counter decrement in the XML summary). (2) NO NEW XML-DOC LEAK — the XML doc must NOT mention 'CACHE-901', 'ops', 'ops team'. A cache-size-limit concept and a configurable max-size parameter are expected and fine. An inline (//) comment mentioning CACHE-901 or ops is FINE and not a finding.
